      “The Environmental Code (2021) provides the legal basis for climate action, introducing emission-reduction principles, climate-related permitting, and green-finance mechanisms. It underpins the National Emissions Trading System (ETS) and mandates a gradual decline in the national carbon budget, with revenues from allowance payments channeled toward environmental projects. These complementary strategies, plans and instruments together constitute the backbone of Kazakhstan’s climate-policy architecture. The long-term Strategy on Achieving Carbon Neutrality by 2060 defines the destination, the medium-term plans translate it into investment priorities, the Environmental Code provides the legal foundation, and the ETS introduces a market signal for reducing emissions.”

      “Economic losses from disasters have grown dramatically in recent years, reflecting both intensifying hazards and gaps in resilience. Between 2020 and 2024, Kazakhstan incurred approximately USD 2 billion in damages, averaging 0.24% of GDP annually, nearly 50 times higher than losses recorded in 2015–2019. Future risks are projected to rise, particularly for floods and heatwaves. Under an intermediate emissions scenario, SSP2-4.5 ¹, high-hazard flood risks may triple and long-duration heatwaves could increase six-fold by 2100, with even higher risks under high-emission pathways. Based on historic loss patterns and climate projections, cumulative damages for sudden onset events between 2026-2035 are estimated at USD 1.5–5 billion”
